review_time_definition: Wall-clock from first detailed inspection to submission; includes coordination/tool delays, not independent human labor.

anchors.quote: For an exactly encoded finite column state, a pure Boolean predicate can mark the unique eligible index whose magnitude is no smaller than every competitor and whose index precedes every equal-magnitude competitor. This is structural applicability only: reversible all-candidate comparison, coherent data access, workspace, no-solution handling, exact success semantics, and resource bounds are unresolved, and the predicate cost can eliminate any search benefit.

Conditionally encode one activation of line 13 as a one-hot QUBO over row indices col through n-1. The objective must select the row with greatest abs(rows[i][col]) and, among exactly equal magnitudes, the lowest index. A lexicographic integer score derived from an exact order-preserving representation of finite binary64 magnitudes may supply the linear objective; a squared one-hot constraint requires a penalty proven larger than the complete objective range. Only pivot selection is formulated: singularity checking, swapping, elimination, back substitution, overflow handling, residual diagnostics, and report construction remain classical.

At each activation, encode the dynamically mutated values rows[i][col], along with eligible indices, rather than the original matrix alone. The encoding must preserve Python binary64 absolute-value ordering, equality, signed-zero behavior, and first-index tie resolution. If candidate state is nonfinite or cannot be encoded exactly, execute the original classical selection. Coefficient construction, exact rank conversion, one-hot penalty bounds, coherent loading, workspace, and backend precision remain unresolved obligations.
Any state outside the exact quantum encoding's established domain follows the original classical path.

binding.rationale: Primary QUBO remains unconstructed: rank conversion, coefficient construction and penalty bounds are explicitly unresolved. Separately, the Grover applicability paragraph gives no-smaller-than-every-competitor and earlier-index-on-equality conditions with an explicit finite-column admission. Bind this secondary predicate only, retaining >= and literal not-< readings; competitors exclude the candidate itself. The finite guard applies explicitly to this secondary claim and outside-encoding states are declared classical. Finite agreement would not validate the primary QUBO or execute fallback.

interpretations.meaning: On finite active values, >= every other candidate and precede each equal competitor.
interpretations.expression: all(values[i] >= values[j] for j in indices if j != i) and all(i < j for j in indices if j != i and values[i] == values[j])

interpretations.meaning: On finite active values, not-< every other candidate and precede each equal competitor.
interpretations.expression: not any(values[i] < values[j] for j in indices if j != i) and all(i < j for j in indices if j != i and values[i] == values[j])
